newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere shares up in Beirut heavy demand.
newsitem.headline: Solidere shares up in Beirut heavy demand.

text.p: Solidere shares continued rising in heavy demand on the Beirut Stock on Monday and brokers said the move would take the shares up to $12-$12.5 in the next coming weeks.
Shares of the three banks listed on the exchange were mixed with one rising, one falling and one holding steady.
The LIBX banks index rose 0.15 percent to 138.25. The BLOM general index rose 3.67 percent to 988.92 and the LISPI general index rose 0.69 percent to 87.61.
Solidere A and B shares, trading in heavy demand, closed at $11.5 from $11 on Friday.

"This upward move will bring the share to the $12-$12.5 area in the few coming weeks if not earlier," Nicholas Sawan, Deputy Manager, head of trading at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest told Reuters.

Demand for the shares on Monday's first fixing was 282,870 against a supply of 172,287. Supply of A shares on the second fixing was 100,319 shares against a demand of 251,638. Supply of B shares on that fixing was 19,000 against a demand of 161,244.
The shares had started rising last Tuesday and brokers said the rise was stimulated by a surge of the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London.

"As expected, the shares are going up. The story has turned around completely with few people selling especially the B shares. The shares will keep the upward trend as long as the GDRs are doing well in London," Sawan said.
The GDRs, issued last November at $11.5, soared on the London Stock Exchange last Tuesday to $17.625 from the previous week's $12. They traded on Friday at $16. The exchange was closed on Monday.
Solidere said purchases by U.S. and European emerging market funds were behind the GDR increase.

"Foreign funds are quite impressed with the management of Solidere and overwhelmed by how things are going and they are consequently buying the shares here possibly through gulf partners," Sawan added.
Brokers also said the expected approval of a 25 cents dividend on the share at a shareholders assembly scheduled for May would push prices up.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce steamed ahead, reaching $17 from $16.625. Banque Audi held steady at $20.125 and Bank of Beirut fell to $3.5 from $3.5625.
Turnover in bank shares was 171,053 compared with 123,344 shares on Friday.
Total BSE turnover was 381,790 shares for a value of $3,677,003 compared with 273,095 shares for a value of $2,953,042 on Friday.

Three of the four listed industrials were traded. Ciments Blancs fell to $4.75 from $5 on tunrover of 301 shares. Pipemaker Eternit rose slightlty to $1.875 from $1.8125 while Ciments Libanais held steady at $1.28125.
